text:
Maya R: Heads-up — we're seeing more prod errors when free-tier bursts in us-west. Some requests hit a slow fallback variant and then time out.
Liam W: Seen that. Is it a quota throttle or routing to the wrong variant? Logs show 429 then fallback to q3-small which becomes CPU-bound under concurrency.
Priya K: Current policy in policy-service: free -> region-preferred -> fallback chain [q3-small, q4a], with hard 429 after 100rps per tenant.
Jordan: Can we try a soft-quota mode? Serve above rps but probabilistically downgrade to cheaper variant once median latency > X. Smoother UX than hard 429s.
Sam Ops: Probabilistic fallback worries me for correctness — cheaper models increase hallucination risk. We'll need a strict header to opt-out for critical flows.
Maya R: Agree. Plan: support header x-req-critical: true -> bypass fallback. For others, soft quota with adaptive weights.
Liam W: Telemetry needs to be sharp: tier+region+variant metrics. Fallback_rate, median_latency, p95, error_rate. Our dashboards currently only show global variant splits.
SREBot: deploy.bot: Canary rollout of policy-service v1.9 started by @Jordan.
Priya K: Draft DSL for soft quota (sketch):
```json
{
  "tier": "free",
  "regions": ["us-west", "eu"],
  "quota": {
    "type": "soft",
    "rps": 100,
    "burst": 200,
    "latency_threshold_ms": 600,
    "fallback_policy": {
      "type": "probabilistic",
      "variants": [
        {"model": "q3-small", "weight": 0.6},
        {"model": "q4a", "weight": 0.4}
      ],
      "adaptive": true
    }
  }
}
```
Jordan: I prefer explicit rules over implicit weights. Suggest: threshold-based switch + cooldown window. Adaptive must be driven by clear signals: GPU queue length + tail latency + per-tenant error rate.
Sam Ops: For quota enforcement we also need to decide counters: cross-region consistent counters for hard quotas, eventual consistency ok for soft quotas. Who owns the usage API? Billing? Eng-infra?
Maya R: Proposal: internal API GET /v1/internal/usage?tenant_id=... returns rps and tokens_today. Debate: sync vs eventually-consistent counters.
Liam W: Eventual consistency is acceptable for soft quotas. Hard quotas require a strongly consistent limiter (centralized), which adds latency and complexity.
Priya K: Console UX idea: matrix UI where rows = tiers and cols = regions. Each cell shows primary model + fallback chain and a toggle for soft/hard plus a slider for jitter/probability.
Maya R: Also need per-tenant audit logs showing when fallbacks happened (enterprise compliance request).
Jordan: Action items: 1) Define telemetry schema (Priya + Liam). 2) Prototype soft-quota state machine (Maya + Sam). 3) Console mockups (Jordan). 4) Decide internal usage API consistency (Eng infra).
Sam Ops: Can we run an experiment behind a feature flag for a pilot tenant? Prefer one org in us-west first.
Priya K: I'll add a Grafana panel: fallback_rate by tenant + median latency by variant. Quick win.
Jordan: Need to keep policy JSON backwards-compatible. No breaking changes for Dedicated/Private installs.
Maya R: @Jordan can you loop in billing and eng-infra? @Liam please add trace points for policy_version and fallback_reason on requests.
Liam W: Will do. Adding tracing hooks and a small log field fallback_reason.
Priya K: Note: for Private installs some customers want to self-manage quotas. We'll support policy export/import and a toggle to honor local quota settings.
SREBot: incident.bot: Increased tail-latency alert suppressed for policy-service canary (manual suppress by @Jordan).
Jordan: I'll open a GH issue with the DSL sketch and link to this thread. Keeping notes here as we iterate.
Maya R: Thanks — moving to GH, will follow up on telemetry schema draft.
